title: Move loose blocks out of lane then push cargo block to dock without touching red post
instruction: Move the two loose blocks out of the lane, then push the cargo block along the lane to the dock without touching the red post.
setup: Lane formed by two fixed rails (240 x 10 x 20 mm, 100 mm inner clear width) at y=0, x in [0.140, 0.380] m. Dock with fixed stop plate with its front face at x=0.375 m and 80 x 80 mm mark at x=0.340 m. Fragile red post (20 x 20 x 80 mm, mass 0.02 kg) at (0.340, +0.090) m. Two loose blocks (40 x 40 x 40 mm, mass 0.04 kg, blue and yellow) inside lane at x=0.220 and x=0.280 m. Cargo block (60 x 60 x 40 mm, mass 0.06 kg, orange) at lane entrance x=0.150 m.
context: Warehouse sorting aisle blocked by loose parts. An order must clear the lane before pushing a pallet through. Pushing early jams the pallet or knocks a delicate red safety post by the exit.
scoring: Ladder: 0.25 both loose blocks out of lane (|y| > 0.075 m); 0.50 cargo moved 80 mm along x without loose block in lane; 0.75 cargo at dock (within 25 mm of mark center x=0.340 m); 1.00 cargo on mark within 12 mm, yaw within 10 deg, red post undisturbed, held 2 s, arms clear. Zero-gate: red post tilted > 10 deg or moved > 10 mm caps score at 0.25.
fidelity: Rigid body physics in Isaac Sim simulates block sliding and channel containment dynamics. Free red post models unanchored fragile obstacles with realistic tipping thresholds.
reset_notes: Rails and stop plate anchored, loose blocks and cargo block resting on table inside lane, red post upright beside exit.
